claim: Split-conformal or CQR intervals on top of a gradient-boosting RUL model reach roughly 88-92% empirical coverage at 90% nominal on C-MAPSS (Robinson, IJPHM 2026; Javanmardi & Hüllermeier 2022/2023).
evidence: Primary sources read in full (PDF text extracted locally). (1) Robinson, C. D., "Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Aircraft Engines with Risk-Aware Prediction Intervals via Conformalized Quantile Regression," IJPHM Vol. 17 No. 1, published 2026-04-27, DOI 10.36001/ijphm.2026.v17i1.4724. Abstract: "framework combines a gradient boosting regressor (GBR) for point predictions with asymmetric conformalized quantile regression (CQR)... empirical coverage of 88-92% at 90% nominal coverage." Table 5 PICP: FD001 0.92, FD002 0.91, FD003 0.88, FD004 0.92 (MPIW 47.6/50.7/42.2/58.5). Setup: TSFresh features on 30-cycle windows, PCA + RF feature selection, GBR point model; CQR calibrated on 30% of training engines held out at the engine level; evaluated on the official C-MAPSS test engines; alpha split asymmetrically (r=2 for FD001/FD003, r=3 for FD002/FD004). Conditional coverage (Table 6) mostly 0.87-1.00 with localized under-coverage (FD002 in the (20,40] RUL bin; early-degradation bins in FD001/FD003). The paper tests only asymmetric CQR; it does not itself run plain split-conformal, and the 88-92% figure is a single run (fixed seed), not averaged over splits. (2) Javanmardi & Hüllermeier, "Conformal Prediction Intervals for Remaining Useful Lifetime Estimation," arXiv 2212.14612 (Dec 2022), IJPHM Vol. 14 No. 2, published 2023-07-24, DOI 10.36001/ijphm.2023.v14i2.3417, code at github.com/alireza-javanmardi/conformal-RUL-intervals. They conformalize DCNN and gradient boosting (GB) with SCP, SCP+NNM, nex-SCP, nex-SCP+NNM and CQR, 15 random train/calibration splits, nominal levels 0.75-0.90. They report NO numeric 88-92% figure; coverage is shown only in violin plots (Fig. 4 for GB). Reading Fig. 4 at alpha=0.10: FD001 SCP ~0.90, CQR ~0.87; FD002 SCP ~0.95, CQR ~0.93; FD003 SCP ~0.84 and CQR ~0.85 with very wide split-to-split spread (~0.70-0.95); FD004 SCP ~0.87, CQR ~0.88. Text: "non-exchangeable frameworks outperform other frameworks in terms of average coverages, while CQR has the best performance in terms of average interval widths," and coverage is guaranteed only "under the exchangeability assumption" (C-MAPSS test trajectories are truncated, which motivates their nex-SCP variants).
correction: The 88-92% figure comes solely from Robinson (IJPHM 2026), using asymmetric CQR (quantile gradient-boosting bounds) on top of a GBR point model, with 30% of training engines held out for calibration and PICP of 0.92/0.91/0.88/0.92 on the official FD001-FD004 test sets in a single fixed-seed run. Javanmardi & Hüllermeier (arXiv 2022 / IJPHM 2023) confirm that split-conformal and CQR on gradient boosting are valid on C-MAPSS but report coverage only graphically; for GB at 90% nominal their averages over 15 splits range roughly 0.84-0.95 depending on subset and method, with FD003 undercovering (~0.84-0.85) and large variance, and the non-exchangeable variants covering better than plain SCP/CQR. Accurate statement: "CQR (and to a lesser extent split conformal) over a gradient-boosting RUL model attains marginal coverage near the 90% target on C-MAPSS, roughly 84-95% across subsets in the literature, with Robinson 2026 reporting 88-92% using asymmetric CQR and an engine-level calibration split."
impact_on_candidate: The differentiator survives: near-nominal marginal coverage on held-out engines is demonstrably achievable with an off-the-shelf GBR + CQR pipeline (Robinson's recipe uses only sklearn-style components, TSFresh, and a 30% engine-level calibration split, and Javanmardi's code is public), so a student team can plausibly reproduce it. However, the analysis should (a) attribute 88-92% to Robinson only and cite Javanmardi for validity rather than that number, (b) expect subset-dependent results, with FD003-style undercoverage (~0.84-0.88) and run-to-run variance being realistic rather than a tight 88-92% band, (c) prefer CQR over plain split conformal (fixed-width intervals, weaker on FD003/FD004), and (d) calibrate on held-out engines, not held-out windows, and acknowledge the exchangeability caveat for truncated test trajectories. If judges probe, a single-seed 88-92% claim should be presented as "near-nominal" with a reported PICP per subset, not as a guaranteed range.
